items.rationale: Kimi's October 2023 long-context product identity is structurally important to the family history, but the current Discovery source is a secondary investor account and cannot carry priority or exact technical claims without stronger evidence.

The X signal is useful for discovering runtime/local-inference adoption work around large MoE models, but neither performance values nor ecosystem prevalence can be promoted without authoritative project/repository evidence.
The observed Kimi attribution dispute is material as an ecosystem-friction lead only; it cannot establish infringement, derivative provenance, or license interpretation by itself.

Enterprise origin-policy restrictions are a plausible adoption boundary distinct from capability and license, but the X observation requires non-X corroboration before it can support a general market or enterprise claim.
Yi-1.5 is useful as a 2023-2024 open-weight/local-deployment and coding bridge, but the currently discovered lineage does not support treating Yi as a co-equal 2026 general-frontier endpoint.

Baichuan remains relevant as an early-independent-to-specialized/derivative transition, but the current M3 medical branch should not be presented as a co-equal independent general-frontier model family.
The X runtime-adoption signal lacks primary repository corroboration in the accepted task and cannot support performance, memory, integration-prevalence, or ecosystem-prevalence claims.
The X enterprise-origin-policy observation lacks non-X corroboration and cannot establish prevalence, sector scope, geography, or formal procurement policy.

The X license-friction discussion cannot establish infringement, derivative provenance, applicable version, or legal interpretation; the exact D021 license is the authoritative material artifact instead.

The October 2023 Kimi launch lead is secondary-source only and remains insufficient for an unqualified historical claim; the Architecture will preserve this chronology as an explicit limitation rather than select the source.
